clue.text: Carry out each domestic creature with speed

parts.note: per means each, as in 'a pound per head'
a pet is an animal kept in the home
rate is speed, as in 'at a great rate'

explanation.surface: Someone does a job each time with a household animal, hurrying along.
explanation.definitionFit: To perpetrate is to commit or carry through an act, usually a bad one.

indicators.note: initially, placed before the word put, asks for its opening letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone looks upset from the very start.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the first letter of 'put' then OUT, and to sulk is to appear put out.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushing out the lips is the face of someone who is annoyed or sulking.

parts.note: to rid is to free, as in 'rid the house of mice'
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A journey powered by renewable sources.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride is to journey on a horse, bike or vehicle.

clue.text: Girl's patient translation of great volume

indicators.note: a translation turns words into new form, here a rearrangement of the letters

parts.note: the possessive s is kept as a letter of the fodder
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl's patient renders a big book from another language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volume' suggests a book being translated, but here it means loudness; 'translation' reworks the letters of GIRLS and PATIENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound that seems loud enough to crack the eardrums has enormous loudness.

explanation.surface: A seaman getting a telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Royal Navy a non-commissioned seaman is a rating; a rating is also a scolding or reprimand.

clue.text: Bear child that becomes a hooligan

parts.note: a teddy is a toy bear
a boy is a male child

explanation.surface: A cuddly toy whose young owner grows up to be a thug.
explanation.walkthrough: A TEDDY BOY was a member of a 1950s British youth subculture in Edwardian-style suits, linked in the press with gang violence.
explanation.definitionFit: Teddy boys were 1950s British youths seen as rowdy troublemakers.

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: return asks for the little word of to be turned to run backwards

explanation.surface: A fashionable comeback for short news bulletins.
explanation.definitionFit: Info is a clipped form of information, a short word for news.

indicators.note: to snoop round is to move about, which here moves the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A nosy person poking around a graveyard looking for old remains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' tells you to rework the letters of RELIC and SNOOP; 'Wanting' is a link, the relic being what the snooper wants.
explanation.definitionFit: A necropolis is a large ancient burial ground, literally a city of the dead.

explanation.surface: A horse worn out and then set aside.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse ridden too hard is worn out; a decision overruled by higher authority has been set aside.

clue.text: Fail to learn part properly, as actor?

explanation.surface: A performer who does not know their lines.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as UNDER-STUDY, the word means to study too little; as one word it is a standby performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Studying too little means not learning a role; a stand-in performer learns a lead's role to cover it.

clue.text: Amount of land taken by crusaders

explanation.surface: A plot seized by medieval knights.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land area; Acre is also a port in Israel captured during the Crusades.

clue.text: Working with worry for flourishing business

parts.note: going means working or running, as of a machine
concern means worry or anxiety

explanation.surface: Running a company while anxious about how it is doing.
explanation.definitionFit: A going concern is a firm that is trading successfully and expected to continue.

clue.text: If you annoyingly put trump here, how I may swear

definitions.text: If you annoyingly put trump here, how I may swear

parts.words: If you annoyingly put trump here, how I may swear
parts.note: in card games such as bridge the top cards are honours; trumping a partner's top card lands it on top of that card, and the protest doubles as a solemn oath

explanation.surface: A card player complains bitterly when partner plays a trump on their winner.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge and whist the ace, king, queen, jack and ten are called honours, so the oath is also a literal description of where the trump landed.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an old-fashioned oath meaning 'I swear it is true'.

clue.text: Very tense situation — just the time to take a picture?

definitions.text: just the time to take a picture

explanation.surface: A dramatic moment a photographer would want to capture.
explanation.definitionFit: A flashpoint is where trouble erupts; read literally it is the moment to fire a camera's flash.

clue.text: Kept stew made in a tin

indicators.note: a stew mixes its ingredients together, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Preserved stew prepared in a can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stew' looks like the food being kept but is the signal to rearrange MADE IN A TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To have maintained something is to have kept it going or in good condition.

indicators.note: to means the second piece is added on after the first

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow
a din is a loud unpleasant noise

explanation.surface: Bringing a racket into a quiet field.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead in is to bring in or introduce something, as a presenter leads into a topic.

explanation.surface: A French word meaning a home loan.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: 'mortgage' is a word meaning a loan, and is itself a borrowing from French.
explanation.definitionFit: A term borrowed from another language is a borrowing; taken literally, mortgage is a word for a type of loan.

parts.note: to do is to make, as in 'do a cake'
a native is a local, someone born in the place

explanation.surface: An instruction to make a tip for a neighbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A donative is a gift or present, especially an official one, like a tip.

explanation.surface: Approving a punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction is to permit officially; a sanction is also a punitive measure, as against a country.

indicators.note: about means the two compass points go around the other piece

parts.note: S and E are two compass points, south and east
to crib is to copy someone else's work, and a crib is a piece so copied

explanation.surface: An author making accusations of copying.
explanation.definitionFit: A scribe is someone who writes, originally a copyist of manuscripts.

parts.note: glad means happy

indicators.note: extremely asks for the outermost letters of the word Yes

explanation.surface: A woman asked if she is happy says yes, very much so.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladys is a woman's given name.

parts.note: a prairie schooner was a covered wagon of the American West, which travels across the flat grasslands as a ship moves on water

explanation.surface: A covered wagon rolls smoothly across the American grasslands.
explanation.walkthrough: A prairie schooner was a covered wagon, so its 'sailing' is done over the plains; the phrase also means smooth progress.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a straightforward course with no difficulties.

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A nasty ancient heathen deity.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is an image of a deity worshipped as a god.

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
ay, also spelt aye, is an old word for always or ever

explanation.surface: A dad who is forever getting into fights.
explanation.definitionFit: A fray is a noisy fight or quarrel.

clue.text: Where tourists from Helsinki head off?

indicators.note: head off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: people from Helsinki are Finns

explanation.surface: Asking where visitors from Finland's capital are going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head off' looks like setting out on a trip, but it removes the first letter of FINNS.
explanation.definitionFit: Travellers stay at inns, hotels or pubs offering lodging.

clue.text: Object found by academic who displays uncanny intuition

parts.note: to mind is to object, as in 'do you mind?'
a reader is a senior university lecturer in Britain

explanation.surface: Something discovered by a scholar with a weird gift for insight.
explanation.walkthrough: In British universities a READER is an academic rank just below professor.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who seems to know what others are thinking appears to have a telepathic gift.

explanation.surface: Someone put in an order for a huge amount.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidy means neat and orderly; it also means considerable, as in 'a tidy sum of money'.

clue.text: Learn ploys specially created for me

indicators.note: something specially created is made anew, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Tactics designed with someone in mind to teach them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'specially created' rearranges the letters of LEARN and PLOYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something personally means speaking for oneself, as in 'speaking for myself'.
